original_value: Distance metric learning (DML) has been demonstrated to be successful and essential in diverse applications. Transfer metric learning (TML) can help DML in the target domain with limited label information by utilizing information from some related source domains. The heterogeneous TML (HTML), where the feature representations vary from the source to the target domain, is general and challenging. However, current HTML approaches are usually conducted in a batch manner and cannot handle sequential data. This motivates the proposed online HTML (OHTML) method. In particular, the distance metric in the source domain is pre-trained using some existing DML algorithms. To enable knowledge transfer, we assume there are large amounts of unlabeled corresponding data that have representations in both the source and target domains. By enforcing the distances (between these unlabeled samples) in the target domain to agree with those in the source domain under the manifold regularization theme, we learn an improved target metric. We formulate the problem in the online setting so that the optimization is efficient and the model can be adapted to new coming data. Experiments in diverse applications demonstrate both effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method.

result.paraphrase: Distance metric learning (DML) has proven effective and important across a wide range of applications. Transfer metric learning (TML) can assist DML in a target domain with scarce labels by leveraging knowledge from related source domains. Heterogeneous TML (HTML), in which feature representations differ between source and target domains, is both general and challenging. However, existing HTML methods are typically batch-based and are unable to process sequential data. This limitation motivates the proposed online HTML (OHTML) approach. Specifically, the source-domain distance metric is pretrained with established DML algorithms. For knowledge transfer, we assume the availability of large amounts of unlabeled paired data that are represented in both the source and target domains. By constraining the distances between these unlabeled samples in the target domain to match those in the source domain under a manifold regularization framework, we learn a better target metric. We cast the problem in an online setting to make optimization efficient and allow the model to adapt to newly arriving data. Experiments on diverse applications show that the proposed method is both effective and efficient.
